sourceSpan.excerpt: But but the exercise of that free will is almost moot if we don't know that the choice exists, right? And that's the part that I'm arguing for. aiItem.title: Finite consequences
aiItem.text: Annihilation should follow only persistent refusal of an adequately known relationship, never intellectual failure. Remediable epistemic barriers must therefore be clarified before final loss. Making the option unmistakably available without compelling acceptance distinguishes culpable refusal from sincere inability and answers the known-option objection. That additional constraint makes the comparison more precise and publicly assessable.

aiItem.thesis: Nonresistant nonbelief makes a perfectly loving relational God implausible because freedom cannot explain sincere ignorance of the offered relationship.
premises: Perfect love desiring relationship would ensure every capable person recognizes that the relational option exists.
Knowing an option exists does not coerce acceptance or force loving commitment.
Some sincere seekers remain unconvinced, so widespread theism cannot answer their particular deprivation.
Salvation consequences tied to involuntary belief attach grave stakes to unequal epistemic access.
Uncertainty-produced goods cannot justify hiddenness when less costly arrangements preserve comparable goods.
aiItem.conclusion: Sincere nonbelief remains strong evidence against this God even after replacing torment with annihilation.
